meta.titre: Comparison: comparatives and superlatives in French
meta.sous_theme: Plus, moins, aussi, autant, the superlative, and the irregular forms meilleur and mieux

sections.contenu_markdown: Imagine two stalls in a market in Bamenda that sell the same tomatoes at different prices. You say that one seller is dearer than the other, and that a third one is the cheapest of the market. Comparing people, prices and quantities is something you do every day, and the GCE O Level French tests it in Paper 1. The gap may be in a single sentence or inside a passage with numbered spaces. The right word depends on a few clues that you can learn to read.

items: Adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun (grand, grande, grands, grandes).
Adverbs do not change their form (vite, bien, souvent).
After a quantity word, a noun is used without an article (beaucoup de tomates).

sections.contenu_markdown:
### The comparative

You compare two things or people in three ways: more, less, as much.

| Idea | Adjective or adverb | Noun | Verb |
|---|---|---|---|
| more | plus + adj./adv. + **que** | plus **de** + noun + **que** | verb + plus **que** |
| less | moins + adj./adv. + **que** | moins **de** + noun + **que** | verb + moins **que** |
| equal | aussi + adj./adv. + **que** | autant **de** + noun + **que** | verb + autant **que** |

- *Ce sac est plus lourd que l'autre.* (This bag is heavier than the other.)
- *Elle court aussi vite que son frère.* (She runs as fast as her brother.)
- *J'ai moins de devoirs que toi.* (I have less homework than you.)
- *Il mange autant que son père.* (He eats as much as his father.)

The adjective agrees with the thing described: *Les mangues sont plus sucrées que les oranges.* (The mangoes are sweeter than the oranges.)

### The superlative

The superlative picks one item out of a group: **le / la / les + plus / moins + adjective**. The article agrees with the noun, and the group is usually introduced by **de** (du, de la, des).

- *Ce marché est le plus grand de la ville.* (This market is the biggest in the town.)
- *Les élèves les plus sérieux réussissent.* (The most serious pupils succeed.)

If the adjective comes after the noun, the article is repeated: *la route la plus longue*. With an adverb the article is always *le*: *Cet élève travaille le plus sérieusement.*

### The irregular forms

| Basic word | Comparative | Superlative |
|---|---|---|
| bon (adjective) | meilleur, meilleure | le meilleur, la meilleure |
| bien (adverb) | mieux | le mieux |
| mauvais (adjective) | pire (or plus mauvais) | le pire |

Never say *plus bon* or *plus bien*. *Meilleur* is an adjective and agrees with its noun; *mieux* is an adverb and does not change. The irregular forms exist only for *plus*: *aussi bon*, *moins bon*, *aussi bien* and *moins bien* are correct.

variantes.nom: Spotting the structure in a gap-fill question
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a Paper 1 gap sits in a sentence or a passage that compares two or more things
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Read the words around the gap.

- **que** or **qu'** after the gap: a comparative (*plus ... que*, *aussi ... que*).
- **du / de la / des** + a group after the gap (*du quartier*, *de la classe*): a superlative, so *le / la / les plus* or *moins*.
- An article just before the gap (*la ____*): a superlative (*la plus ...*, *la meilleure*); check the gender.
- The facts of the sentence tell you *plus* or *moins*: a higher price gives *plus cher*, a lower one gives *moins cher*.

Then check the gender and number of the subject, and reread the sentence.

variantes.nom: Quantities: plus de, moins de, autant de
variantes.quand_utiliser: When you compare numbers of things or people
variantes.contenu_markdown:
After *plus de*, *moins de* and *autant de*, the noun has no article: *moins de sucre*, *autant d'élèves* (de becomes d' before a vowel). With a verb, no *de*: *Il travaille plus que moi.*

*Il y a moins d'élèves qu'hier.* (There are fewer pupils than yesterday.) *Cette classe a plus de filles que de garçons.* (This class has more girls than boys.)

sections.enonce_markdown:
Choose the answer that fills the gap: « Le pain du kiosque A coûte 250 FCFA. Dans les autres kiosques, il coûte 200 FCFA. Le kiosque A est ____ du quartier. »

(a) le plus cher (b) la plus chère (c) plus cher (d) aussi cher

etapes.resultat_markdown: 250 FCFA is more than 200 FCFA, so kiosk A is dearer than all the others.

etapes.action: Study the words after the gap.
etapes.justification: *Du quartier* names the group in which one item is picked out, which is the sign of a superlative.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A superlative is needed: le/la/les + plus + adjective.

etapes.justification: The article agrees with the noun *kiosque*, which is masculine singular.
(b) is feminine. (c) has no article and would need *que* after it. (d) means "equally dear", which contradicts the prices.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Le kiosque A est le plus cher du quartier.* (Kiosk A is the dearest in the area.)

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **(a) le plus cher**. The method: read the facts to choose *plus* or *moins*, read what follows the gap to recognise a superlative, then match the article with the gender and number of the subject.

items.erreur_markdown: *Ce riz est plus bon que l'autre.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: The comparative of the adjective *bon* is irregular: *plus bon* does not exist.
items.correction_markdown: *Ce riz est **meilleur** que l'autre.* (This rice is better than the other.)

items.pourquoi_faux: *Chante* is a verb, so an adverb is needed. *Meilleur* is an adjective. The comparative of the adverb *bien* is *mieux*.
items.correction_markdown: *Elle chante **mieux** que moi.* (She sings better than I do.)

items.erreur_markdown: *Ma sœur est plus grande de moi.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: The second term of a comparative is introduced by *que*, never by *de*.
items.correction_markdown: *Ma sœur est plus grande **que** moi.* (My sister is taller than I am.)

items.erreur_markdown: *Cette route est le plus longue du village.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: The article of a superlative agrees with the noun. *Route* is feminine.
items.correction_markdown: *Cette route est **la** plus longue du village.* (This road is the longest in the village.)

items.erreur_markdown: *Il y a moins des élèves qu'hier.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: After *moins de* the noun has no article, so *des* is wrong.
items.correction_markdown: *Il y a moins **d'**élèves qu'hier.* (There are fewer pupils than yesterday.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Fill each gap.

(a) Le lion est ____ rapide ____ la tortue.

(b) Paul et son frère ont tous les deux quatorze ans. Paul est ____ âgé ____ son frère.

(c) Ma classe compte quarante élèves, la tienne en compte cinquante. Ma classe a ____ élèves que la tienne.

(d) Choose *meilleur(e)* or *mieux*: Cette mangue est ____ que celle-là. Mon frère dessine ____ que moi.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **plus ... que**. The lion is faster: *Le lion est plus rapide que la tortue.*

(b) **aussi ... que**. They have the same age: *Paul est aussi âgé que son frère.*

(c) **moins d'**. 40 is less than 50, and the noun follows without an article: *Ma classe a moins d'élèves que la tienne.*

(d) **meilleure**, then **mieux**. *Mangue* is a feminine noun, so the adjective *meilleure* is used: *Cette mangue est meilleure que celle-là.* *Dessine* is a verb, so the adverb: *Mon frère dessine mieux que moi.*

items.enonce_markdown:
Awa is 1.70 m tall, Julie 1.65 m and Rose 1.60 m. Three pieces of cloth cost 3000 FCFA (A), 2000 FCFA (B) and 2500 FCFA (C). Fill each gap with the right superlative.

(a) Awa est ____ des trois.

(b) Rose est ____ des trois.

(c) Le tissu B est ____ des trois.

(d) Paul court ____ de tous les élèves. (He is faster than all of them.)

(e) Marie a les notes les plus élevées : c'est ____ élève de la classe.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **la plus grande**. 1.70 m is the highest, and *Awa* is feminine.

(b) **la plus petite**. 1.60 m is the lowest.

(c) **le moins cher**. 2000 FCFA is the lowest price, and *tissu* is masculine.

(d) **le plus vite**. With an adverb the article is always *le*: *Paul court le plus vite de tous les élèves.*

(e) **la meilleure**. The best marks make her the best pupil, and *élève* is feminine here: *c'est la meilleure élève de la classe.*

items.enonce_markdown:
A table shows tomatoes in three market stalls.

| Stall | Price per kilo | Customers per day |
|---|---|---|
| A | 800 FCFA | 30 |
| B | 600 FCFA | 50 |
| C | 700 FCFA | 40 |

Write four correct French sentences:

(a) compare the prices of A and B with *plus ... que*;

(b) say which stall is the cheapest of the three;

(c) compare the customers of A and C with *moins de ... que*;

(d) compare the customers of B and C with *plus de ... que*.

(e) Explain why the adjective is feminine plural in your sentence (a).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Les tomates de A sont plus chères que celles de B.** 800 is more than 600.

(b) **Les tomates de B sont les moins chères des trois.** 600 FCFA is the lowest price.

(c) **A a moins de clients que C.** 30 is less than 40; no article after *moins de*.

(d) **B a plus de clients que C.** 50 is more than 40.

(e) The adjective *chères* agrees with the subject *les tomates*, which is feminine plural.

items_markdown: Comparative: **plus / moins / aussi + adjective or adverb + que**; with nouns **plus de / moins de / autant de + noun + que**.
The second term of a comparison is introduced by **que**, not by *de*. After *plus de, moins de, autant de* the noun has no article.
Superlative: **le / la / les + plus / moins + adjective**, with the group introduced by *de* (du, de la, des). The article agrees with the noun and is repeated after the noun.
With an adverb the superlative is always **le plus / le moins**.
Irregular: **bon** gives **meilleur(e)**, **bien** gives **mieux**. Never *plus bon* or *plus bien*.
In a gap-fill question, read the words after the gap (*que*, *du quartier*), the article before it, and the facts that decide between *plus* and *moins*.
